title: Foundations: Celtic Folk - The Complete Guide
summary: What Celtic Folk is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Celtic Folk songs: Celtic folk songs carry the music of Ireland and Scotland: modal melodies, jigs and reels, rebel songs and emigrant laments, sung with ornamented, sean-nós-style phrasing.

History: Irish traditional music survived in kitchens and pubs through the 19th century; collectors like Edward Bunting (1792) preserved harp tunes. The Dubliners, The Chieftains, and Clancy Brothers carried it worldwide in the 1960s.

How the songs work: Celtic Folk favors the keys of G, D, Em, Am, Bm. Common forms include Air (slow, free rhythm) then dance set; Rebel ballad with singalong chorus. Players should master dadgad tuning for drone-rich accompaniment first, then ornamentation: cuts, rolls, and slides on melody notes. DADGAD tuning is the Celtic guitarist's home base.

title: Scarborough Fair - Complete Public-Domain Song
summary: Full lyrics and playing guide for Scarborough Fair, a public-domain Celtic Folk standard.
body:
Scarborough Fair (Traditional English ballad. Public domain.) is public domain, so this record carries the complete lyrics — sing it, teach it, record it freely.

COMPLETE LYRICS:
Are you going to Scarborough Fair?
Parsley, sage, rosemary and thyme;
Remember me to one who lives there,
She once was a true love of mine.

Tell her to make me a cambric shirt,
Parsley, sage, rosemary and thyme;
Without no seams nor needlework,
Then she'll be a true love of mine.

Tell her to find me an acre of land,
Parsley, sage, rosemary and thyme;
Between the salt water and the sea strand,
Then she'll be a true love of mine.

Tell her to reap it with a sickle of leather,
Parsley, sage, rosemary and thyme;
And gather it all in a bunch of heather,
Then she'll be a true love of mine.

HOW TO PLAY IT: a Celtic Folk accompaniment in G using the 'Dorian air Em–D' pattern:
Gm | F | Gm | F

Technique: dadgad tuning for drone-rich accompaniment. DADGAD tuning is the Celtic guitarist's home base.
facts: Form: Air (slow, free rhythm) then dance set

title: Greensleeves - Complete Public-Domain Song
summary: Full lyrics and playing guide for Greensleeves, a public-domain Celtic Folk standard.
body:
Greensleeves (Traditional English, 16th century (registered 1580). Public domain.) is public domain, so this record carries the complete lyrics — sing it, teach it, record it freely.

COMPLETE LYRICS:
Alas, my love, you do me wrong,
To cast me off discourteously.
For I have loved you well and long,
Delighting in your company.

Chorus:
Greensleeves was all my joy,
Greensleeves was my delight,
Greensleeves was my heart of gold,
And who but my lady Greensleeves.

I have been ready at your hand,
To grant whatever you would crave;
I have both wagered life and land,
Your love and good-will for to have.

HOW TO PLAY IT: a Celtic Folk accompaniment in D using the 'Rebel song I–VII–I' pattern:
D | C | D | G

Technique: ornamentation: cuts, rolls, and slides on melody notes. DADGAD tuning is the Celtic guitarist's home base.
